# SEO

Curated by Skill Harbor: a no-gimmicks SEO skill built on technical correctness, performance, and content relevance. It audits in a fixed order: technical blockers first (robots.txt allowing the right pages, no accidental noindex, shallow click depth, no redirect chains over two hops, self-consistent canonicals), then indexability (consistent URL format, correct hreflang, sitemaps matching the intended public surface), then performance (LCP under 2.5s, INP under 200ms, CLS under 0.1, with the common fixes spelled out), then structured data matched to reality (Organization, Article, Product and Offer, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage only when the content truly matches), then on-page rules (50 to 60 character titles with the keyword up front, honest 120 to 160 character meta descriptions, one clear H1, real heading hierarchy), then keyword mapping (one primary intent per URL, intent match over volume, cannibalization detection) and internal linking (strong pages feeding target pages, descriptive anchors). Every finding ships in a fixed shape: severity, location, issue, fix. The anti-pattern table is the philosophy: no keyword stuffing, no thin near-duplicates, no schema for content that isn't there, no advice without reading the actual page, no generic "improve SEO" outputs untied to a page or asset. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: it advises from what you show it; point it at real URLs or paste the actual...
